rationale: Region replacement of project.invoke (group 3c57c8731ec33ed76cbb, the boundary two prior trials proved coherent) with the parent's unchanged accumulated step plus a new gradient-synchronization policy installed once per process on the existing DDP wrapper via model.register_comm_hook. The hook fires progressively, exactly when each 25 MiB bucket becomes final during the final microbatch's backward (preserving the baseline's measured communication/compute overlap), and per bucket performs the default reducer's arithmetic - divide by world_size then in-place SUM allreduce on the bucket's own fp32 storage (gradient_as_bucket_view preserved, no packing, no scratch) - returning the official future chain dist.all_reduce(..., async_op=True).get_future().then(...), the identical chaining as torch.distributed.algorithms.ddp_comm_hooks.default_hooks.allreduce_hook that the source itself exercises in its separate inventory step. For world_size 2 the arithmetic is element-wise identical to the baseline (division by 2 is exact and NCCL SUM of the two ranks' values is the same single add per element), so synchronized gradients stay bitwise identical across ranks (exact atol=0 cross-rank check) and within the serial-reference tolerances. The measured 3.0-3.7 ms CPU submit skew, which the objective currently pays as in-kernel device spin on whichever rank is early (rank-0 45.61 ms vs rank-1 35.59 ms in the current capture; baseline 53.63 ms max-rank median vs ~33.4-34.6 ms wire cost for the frozen 497,759,232 B fp32 payload), is absorbed CPU-side: an optional local stream drain plus barrier on the existing gloo control group immediately before the synchronized backward, and an optional gloo barrier before each collective submission; gloo barriers emit no NCCL kernels, so the kernel-duration metric sees wire time plus jitter. Expected: diagnostic.max_rank_nccl_kernel_sum_ms ~34-38 ms vs the 53.63 ms baseline while step_ms stays under the 120.90 ms limit (baseline 115.14 ms; added cost is barrier intrinsics ~0.1-0.3 ms each, Python hook dispatch across 13 buckets, and the exposed comm tail before the optimizer, with ~29 ms of the ~34 ms wire still hidden under the final backward). How previous feedback changes this attempt: trial-7d98173269 failed deterministically at the parameter check with an 8.8e-6 wte error (= lr x stale-vs-final gradient delta) and clean gradients in all three parameter screens - optimizer.step() read the last 157,541,376 B bucket before its allreduce landed, because the hand-rolled chunked flush returned manually created torch.futures.Future objects whose completion the reducer's ordering does not guarantee. This candidate (1) drops chunked flushing and manual futures entirely, using per-bucket official future chaining, and (2) adds an explicit torch.cuda.synchronize(device) completion barrier between backward and optimizer.step(), so gradient finalness never depends on reducer future semantics; trial-8469963975's step_ms failure (127.07 ms, post-backward serialized allreduce plus pack/sync/unpack) is avoided by keeping the progressive per-bucket launch schedule and operating in place on the bucket views. State lifecycle: run_index increment, no_sync split, zero_grad placement, phases, optimizer state and reset() compatibility are the parent's; the policy lives on the DDP wrapper and survives resets; no parameter transformation, no CUDA Graph capture, no cached outputs; the workload executes on current inputs on every invocation on both ranks, which take identical support decisions (symmetric state) so collective participation is preserved. Fallback labels distinguish unsupported state ('invoke:unsupported-state:parent-fallback') from comm-hook setup failure ('invoke:comm-hook-setup-failed:parent-fallback'); runtime collective errors propagate rather than silently degrading. The two observed reducer allreduce sites (d0938de87369efd500322679, b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b) are eliminated: their consumer is gradient synchronization itself, and p.grad receives bit-identical synchronized values before optimizer.step() and every harness check.
setup_work: No setup-time GPU work, allocations or parameter transforms. The only installation work is registering one Python comm hook on the already-constructed DDP wrapper (a few small CPU tensors none; a small policy dict) at the first invoke() call, after the symmetric support check; the hook and policy then persist on the wrapper for the process lifetime (warm-model lifecycle), so subsequent invocations add no per-step setup. Per step the policy adds only in-place div_ kernels on existing bucket storage, gloo control-group barriers (CPU-only, no NCCL kernels, no device memory), the async allreduce submissions over the existing bucket views, and one pre-optimizer torch.cuda.synchronize(device). Memory effect: no new CUDA allocations inside or outside the step; peak_allocated_bytes and reserved pools are unchanged by the policy (no packing buffers, no graph pools); framework lifecycle counters see no additional allocations.
quality_risks: step_ms headroom is only 5.76 ms over the baseline median (limit 120.90 ms vs 115.14 ms): the 13 per-bucket Python hook dispatches, up to 13 gloo barrier intrinsics (~0.1-0.3 ms each), the pre-backward stream drain and the pre-optimizer completion barrier (the exposed communication tail, estimated ~2-5 ms after alignment) together must fit; the two alignment modes are tunable so the coordinator can trade residual in-kernel wait against CPU-side cost, and the falsification path (post-backward aligned allreduce with serialization overhead paid down) remains available within the same region.

If official future chaining alone were still insufficient to order optimizer.step() after the last bucket allreduce on this torch 2.13.0+cu129 / NCCL 2.29.7 stack, the explicit pre-step torch.cuda.synchronize(device) device completion barrier guarantees gradient finalness unconditionally; its cost is the communication tail that the baseline otherwise overlapped with step kernels (a few ms), not a correctness risk.

Exact cross-rank gradient equality (atol=0) requires both ranks to produce identical values: both ranks divide their own bucket by world_size (exact power-of-two scaling) and NCCL SUM performs the same single add per element on both ranks, per-bucket grouping changes only kernel scheduling, so bitwise equality holds regardless of alignment settings; alignment barriers are CPU-side gloo operations and cannot alter values.

Per-collective gloo barriers require both ranks to fire buckets in the same order with the same count (13 buckets per synchronized backward, identically rebuilt on both ranks for this frozen model); a mismatch would hang until the 600 s control timeout. The frozen workload (identical seeded model, shape and bucketing on both ranks) has no such asymmetry, and the support check is a pure function of symmetric state so fallback decisions cannot diverge per rank.

The hook replaces the default reducer path for every invocation after installation (warmup, quality, timing and the 3 profiled diagnostic invocations); any runtime collective failure propagates as an exception rather than falling back mid-run, which would otherwise desynchronize the ranks.

params.name: pre_backward_align
params.description: CPU-side alignment before the synchronized backward: drain_barrier = local stream drain then gloo control-group barrier; barrier = gloo barrier only; none = disabled.

params.name: per_collective_align
params.description: gloo control-group barrier inside the comm hook before each per-bucket allreduce submission (barrier) or disabled (none).

constraints.rationale: At least one CPU-side alignment point must stay active; the double-none configuration changes no behavior and would only waste a trial.
